redaction_note: Kubernetes context names are replaced with role placeholders. An earlier revision of this file named the reachable context literally; it is a live infrastructure identifier and this repository is public, so it should not have been committed. Recorded here rather than silently rewritten, because the working-tree fix does not remove it from public history and the record of what was exposed is what an owner needs.

the_gate_that_remains.first_error: execution preflight cluster_owner: raw/runtime submit requires one explicit Kubernetes context; ambient context is not execution evidence
the_gate_that_remains.second_error_with_the_context_supplied: No NPA cluster identity exists for context '<reachable-context>'; refusing controller adoption.
the_gate_that_remains.what_would_clear_it: Either the controller-owner context added to this machine's kubeconfig, or an NPA cluster identity registered for the reachable context through the supported provisioning or adoption path. Both are operator actions.
the_gate_that_remains.why_it_is_a_real_wall: The two requirements are satisfied by disjoint sets here. The reachable context is in kubeconfig and is referenced by a project's k8s_context, but the config's clusters map is empty, so no NPA cluster identity exists under that name. The context that does carry an identity, as the recorded SkyPilot controller owner, is absent from kubeconfig. Neither can be made to satisfy both from this lane: registering a cluster identity to satisfy the guard would be defeating a controller-adoption safety check rather than passing it, and that is not a thing to do to make a run start.

what_was_previously_recorded_as_the_bloc: 'The npa.workflow runtime path needs one Kubernetes context that is both in kubeconfig and carries an NPA cluster identity under that context name.' That was recorded without having reproduced it. It is now reproduced exactly, and most of the path around it turned out to be open.
